Dual-Mode van der Waals Ferroelectrics for Hybrid Analog-Digital In-Memory Computing

Case ID:
UA27-057
Web Published:
10/1/2026
Invention:

This technology is a new van der Waals device structure that realizes analog-digital dual-mode operation and provides a potential route towards balancing energy efficiency and update precision in adaptive in-memory computing. It combines two physically distinct ferroelectric mechanisms unique to two-dimensional materials, realizing not merely two polarizations, but the coexistence of two types of ferroelectricity of qualitatively different character, independently addressed by separate gates. The device achieves nanosecond programming, ultralow energy, and hundreds of analog states. Simulations on measured characteristics show reduced energy with preserved accuracy compared to purely analog hardware.

Background: 
Adapting large pretrained models to task- or user-specific settings is a pressing challenge for energy-constrained edge AI. Efficient adaptation requires both the precision of digital hardware and the parallelism of analog hardware, yet existing devices face an accuracy-energy tradeoff, capturing both only at the cost of increased footprint, separate memory elements, or greater circuit complexity. Dual-mode van der Waals ferroelectric devices address these limitations by enabling hybrid analog-digital in-memory computing within a single platform, reducing data movement between memory and computation while supporting efficient, low-power adaptation for data-intensive and edge AI applications.

Applications: 

  • Adaptive AI systems
  • Machine learning inference
  • Data-intensive computing


Advantages: 

  • Lower energy consumption
  • Does not require separate memory elements
  • Supports hybrid analog-digital computing
  • Achieves nanosecond programming
